sections.heading: How to Play Devastation
sections.body:
[h2 type=bar toc="How to Play Devastation"][color=c13]Devastation Evoker Rotation in Midnight Season 2[/color][/h2]
Devastation Evoker is a fairly simple and straightforward with its spell priority. Cooldowns are mostly used on cooldown, while building and spending [resource=19] / [spell=359618].


[wrapper width=1100px][box border=true]
[center]
[table style=grid][tr][td]
	[table]
	[tr]
[td width=6%][icon name=ability_evoker_disintegrate size=medium type=round color=c13 inline=true][/icon][/td]
	[td][b][color=evoker]Build and Spend:[/color][/b] [spell=356995] and [spell=357211] spend [resource=19], primary resource for Evokers. [spell=361469] and [spell=362969] are the filler spells that generate [spell=359618], a proc that allows you to use these abilities without spending Essence. Spend Essence and Essence Burst, then use filler spells while waiting.
	[/td]
	[/tr]
	[/table]
[hr]
	[table]
	[tr]
	[td width=6%][icon name=ability_evoker_dragonrage size=medium type=round color=c13 inline=true][/icon][/td]
	[td][b][color=evoker]Use cooldowns frequently:[/color][/b] [spell=375087] and [spell=357210] (Scalecommander) are Devastation's main cooldown. Essence Burst is guaranteed from filler spells during this buff. Its duration can be extended by both [spell=359073] and [spell=357208] with [spell=375797]. Given that both spells also come with their own short cooldowns, consider what is available when entering Dragonrage and to press them on cooldown during it. 
	[/td]
	[/tr]
	[/table]
[hr]
	[table]
	[tr]
[td width=6%][icon name=ability_evoker_livingflame size=medium type=round color=c13 inline=true][/icon][/td]
	[td][b][color=evoker]Always be casting:[/color][/b] Try to maintain high uptime on targets. Constant use of damaging spells is the key to high damage in Raid and Mythic+. Use [spell=358267] effectively to cast spells on the move. Try to fill "downtime" in your rotation with spells, even if its not completely optimal (Azure Strike for instance). Using [i]something[/i] is almost always better than being idle. Try to use cooldowns and Empowered spells early and often.[/td]
	[/tr]
	[/table]
[/td][/tr][/table]
[/center]
[/box][/wrapper]
[pad]
[center][cta-button guide=32955 icon=classicon_evoker_devastation]Devastation Evoker Starter Guide[/cta-button][/center]

sections.heading: Rotation Priority
sections.body:
[h2 type=bar toc="Rotation Priority"][icon name=classicon_evoker_devastation type=round size=medium inline=true color=c13][/icon] Best Devastation Evoker Rotation[/h2]
Hero talents also add some flavor to the rotation. [color=#539595]Scalecommander[/color] uses [spell=357210] and [color=[symbol=wow-hero-talent-flameshaper] [color=#c03e4e]Flameshaper[/color][/color] monitors [spell=357208]. Aside from this, they mostly play the same.


Below, we break down the main priority lists for Devastation Evoker: Single-Target Rotation, AoE Rotation, and your opener sequence.
[wrapper width=70%][center][box border=true]
	[center][large][b][color=white]Hero Talent Master Switches[/color][/b][/large]
	[pad]
	You can use the master switches below to flip the [b][i]entire page's[/i][/b] options to your selected choice.[/center]

	[wrapper width=95%]

			[display-option="flameshaper" radio="Hero" icon=inv_shadowflames_wave ]Flameshaper[/display-option]
		[/grid]
	[/wrapper]
	[/center]
[/box][/center][/wrapper]
[br]
[tabs name="Rotations" uniform=true]

[spell=358267] can be cast while casting, and allows you to cast while moving. With [spell=441257], a [spell=358267] charge resets with each [spell=357210]. The [spell=358267] buff grows in duration with each cast, so be sure to spend a [spell=358267] charge before each [spell=441257].

[spell=357210] is very strong and should be used on cooldown, but you don't want to stay in the animation longer than needed. Use the [spell=357210] cancel macro found on the [url guide=17792]macros page[/url]. Here's an example of the macro for [spell=356995]:
[code]#showtooltip Disintegrate
/cancelaura Deep Breath
/cast Disintegrate
[/code]
This macro will end your [spell=357210] with the first press and use [spell=356995] with the second. You would tap it twice, right as you hit your target.

[spell=361469] with [spell=369939] can grant two [spell=369297], even in Single Target. This is because the bonus [spell=361469] will try to heals allies if no enemies are available.

sections.heading: Major Cooldowns
sections.body:
[h2 toc="Major Cooldowns" type=bar][color=c13][icon name=classicon_evoker_devastation type=round size=medium inline=true color=c13][/icon] Devastation Evoker Major Cooldowns[/color][/h2]
Devastation Evoker has one main cooldown: [spell=375087]. Other cooldowns are minor, or group buffs. The below section covers [i]how[/i] they work, and most importantly, how to get the most out of each use.
[pad]

[tabs name="cds" uniform=true iconborders=true]
[tab name="Dragonrage" icon=ability_evoker_dragonrage]



	[h3 type=bar toc=false][color=c13] Dragonrage [/color][/h3]
[spell=375087] is your main cooldown as Devastation. This buff guarantees [spell=359618] procs from [spell=361469] and [spell=362969] for the duration. Try to use it every 2 minutes.

Other key takeaways are:
[ul]

[li]Activating this spell fires 3 [spell=357211]s at random targets.[/li]
[li]Gain the full effect of [spell=362980] with [spell=376888].[/li]
[li][spell=357208] and [spell=359073] extend the buff with [spell=375797].[/li]

[li][spell=375087] can be held for AoE, but it is a fairly long buff. The average duration should be around 32 seconds with proper play.[/li]
[li]Apex talents ([spell=1271788]) buff your damage during and after this buff.
[ul][li]After the buff expires, it turns into [spell=1292321] (if running the talent). This spell does AoE damage and grants [spell=369297]. It can only be used 4 times.[/li][/ul][/li]

[/ul]



 



[pad]
[/tab]
[tab name="Empower Spells" icon=ability_evoker_firebreath]

	[h3 type=bar toc=false][color=c13] Empower Spells[/color][/h3]

[spell=357208] and [spell=359073] are Devastation's Empower spells. These can be ranked up for different effects.

Empowering [spell=357208] moves damage from the debuff it applies into the initial hit of upfront damage. [spell=369939] also increases in target count per Empower level. The DoT component from [spell=357208] scales dynamically with [spell=362980], which means that the damage goes down as the target loses health. 


Empowering [spell=359073] increases the target count, and has an affect on damage talents like [spell=1265802]. [spell=375757] doubles the target count per level. 


[hr]
[pad]
For [symbol=wow-hero-talent-flameshaper] [color=#c03e4e]Flameshaper[/color], [spell=357208] and [spell=359073] (without [spell=370553]) should generally be used at rank 1. You can uprank [spell=359073] based on your target count in AoE, but the difference in damage is minor. 
[ul][li]
[spell=357208] has two charges.[/li]
[li]
[spell=444088] uses [spell=357208]  to fuel explosions. This chips away at remaining duration.[/li][/ul]

For [symbol=wow-hero-talent-scalecommander] [color=#539595]Scalecommander[/color], [spell=357208] (without [spell=370553]) and [spell=359073] should generally be used at rank 1. You can uprank based on your target count in AoE, but the difference in damage is minor. 
[ul][li]
Each use of Empowered spells will enable [spell=436335].[/li]
[li][spell=436335] marks the target for [spell=434300]. This enables a damage proc for you and allies.[/li][/ul]

[pad]
[/tab]

[tab name="Tip The Scales" icon=ability_evoker_tipthescales]
	[h3 type=bar toc=false][color=c13] Tip The Scales[/color][/h3]


[spell=370553] is a minor cooldown. It is used in [spell=375087] to instantly cast [spell=359073] or [spell=357208] at max rank. 

[hr]
[pad]
For [symbol=wow-hero-talent-flameshaper] [color=#c03e4e]Flameshaper[/color], [spell=370553] should only be used on [spell=359073]. Higher [spell=357208] uptime is better for [spell=370819], [spell=375801] procs, [spell=357208] damage via [spell=386283], and [spell=444088].

For [symbol=wow-hero-talent-scalecommander] [color=#539595]Scalecommander[/color], [spell=370553] should be used on [spell=359073], but using it on [spell=357208] does not come with a massive penalty. 





[pad]
[/tab]


[tab name="Deep Breath" icon=ability_evoker_deepbreath]
	[h3 type=bar toc=false][color=c13]Deep Breath[/color][/h3]


[spell=357210] is another notable cooldown. This spell always gets full [spell=362980] value with [spell=376888]. Optimal usage depends on your Hero Talents, but it can also be used for movement or to avoid/break crowd control (stuns and roots). Always use [spell=357210] at minimum range unless you need it for movement. [b]It is important to remember that while flying, effects on the ground will still hit you, and you will be locked into the animation.[/b] Some class talents modify this ability:

[ul]
[li][spell=370781] gives you a short buff that decreases [resource=19] costs and increases damage.[/li]
[li][spell=1266151] increases damage and allows for a second use.[/li]
[li][spell=386348] reduces the cooldown.[/li]
[li][spell=410352] takes any damage taken during the skill and stretches it out, adding some safety. [/li]
[/ul]


[hr]
[pad]
[symbol=wow-hero-talent-scalecommander] [color=#539595]Scalecommander[/color] uses this spell on cooldown, due to talents like [spell=433871] and [spell=1260745]. This version of [spell=357210] can be steered, and you can eject from it.
[ul][li]Cooldown is further reduced by [spell=434300] procs via [spell=441206].[/li]
[li]Your Z-axis is preserved during this spell, so long as you don't fly uphill. Use height to your advantage if you plan to fly over rocky or dangerous terrain.[/li][/ul] 
[symbol=wow-hero-talent-flameshaper] [color=#c03e4e]Flameshaper[/color] does not typically use [spell=357210] for damage, unless talents like [spell=370781] are taken.





[pad]
[/tab]


[tab name="Fury of the Aspects" icon=ability_evoker_furyoftheaspects]
	[h3 type=bar toc=false][color=c13]Fury of the Aspects[/color][/h3]



[spell=390386] is a group cooldown, which means that when to use it is often a group decision. This spell grants you and your allies the [spell=2825] effect, increasing your Haste. This spell is off the global cooldown. 

[spell=390386] applies the [spell=57723] debuff, locking players out of receiving similar effects for 10 minutes.


[/tab]

[/tabs]

sections.heading: Advanced Tips
sections.body:
[h2 toc="Advanced Tips" type=bar][color=c13][icon name=Inv_artifact_tome01 type=round size=medium inline=true color=c13][/icon] Devastation Evoker Advanced Tips[/color][/h2]
The best thing you can do to improve your damage as a Devastation Evoker is to [u]always be casting[/u]. Idle time in combat, caused by inactivity or poor movement, adds up and will greatly affect your damage. Mastering movement with [spell=358267] and keeping focus during combat is unequivocally the best way to raise your damage.
[pad]

[tabs name="advanced" uniform=true iconborders=true]
[tab name="Hover and Movement" icon=ability_evoker_hover]
	[h3 type=bar toc=false][color=c13] Hover and Movement [/color][/h3]
[spell=358267] is your most important tool for minimizing damage losses due to movement. [spell=358267] can be cast while casting, and allows you to cast on the move. Subsequent [spell=358267] casts add to the duration, meaning you can use it again while the buff is up without wasting duration. Any time you cancel a cast because you needed to move, it created a small period of downtime. These add up and greatly reduce your damage.

[spell=358733] is also very useful for movement, since using it is much faster than running. Simply tap your spacebar for a boost. Keep in mind, this will not work during normal casts. The trick with [spell=358733] is to triple tap, since canceling it removes the slowfall effect. This makes you travel faster, and hit the ground quicker. Bonus tip: Some ground effects can be avoided if you are at the height of your [spell=358733].

Another interesting quirk of [spell=358267] is that it allows you to [spell=358733] while channeling [spell=356995]. This is very powerful, since it allows you to quickly reposition by tapping your spacebar. Combine [spell=358267] with [spell=358733] canceling to quickly hop around the battlefield while channeling.

Not all downtime is created equal. During [spell=375087], stakes are higher. As [color=#539595]Scalecommander[/color], getting full value from [spell=436335] is also very important. For these reasons, I recommend always having a [spell=358267] in hand for cooldowns. [color=#539595]Scalecommander[/color] has a much easier time with [spell=358267], since each [spell=357210] refunds a charge via [spell=441257]. Make sure you make room for this ahead of time, or the value is wasted. 



Aside from [spell=359073] and [spell=357208], all spells can be cast on the move with [spell=358267].


[/tab]
[tab name="Deep Breath Z-axis" icon=ability_evoker_deepbreath]
	[h3 type=bar toc=false][color=c13] Deep Breath Z-axis[/color][/h3]
As [color=#539595]Scalecommander[/color], [spell=357210] works a bit differently due to [spell=433871]. One interesting property is that it preserves your Z-axis while you are flying. This can be good or bad, depending on the situation. A common situation you want to avoid is using [spell=357210] uphill. Once you start scraping the ground, even a pebble can stop you in your tracks. Instead, try to gain the high ground before using [spell=357210].

Another trick is to [spell=358733] to gain altitude before [spell=357210]. This helps greatly on level surfaces, since even a little added height often allows you to fly over obstacles that would normally stop you in your tracks. In some cases, added height also allows you to avoid damage ground mechanics.

[spell=358267] and [spell=357210] can also be used in tandem to cross great distances in the air. You can try this yourself: Start by jump [spell=358733]ing from a high place. Use both [spell=358267] charges to dash forward twice, then use [spell=357210] until it expires. [spell=357210] again, then [spell=358267] forward twice using the refunds from [spell=441257]. [spell=374968] for one last forward [spell=358267], then finish by reactivating [spell=358733]. In total, this is around 200 yards of movement with minimal loss of height.

[/tab]
[tab name="Disintegrate Chaining and Clipping" icon=ability_evoker_disintegrate]
	[h3 type=bar toc=false][color=c13] Disintegrate Chaining and Clipping [/color][/h3]



[spell=356995] has 5 ticks with [spell=1219723] and 4 ticks without. If channeling [spell=356995], you can cast [spell=356995] again after the 4th tick without losing damage. This causes the new [spell=356995] to chain in a similar "Pandemic" fashion and moves remaining duration and final tick of the previous channel to the new one. This is chaining, and you don't lose any value doing this. As a general rule, you always want to avoid downtime by chaining [spell=356995] after the penultimate tick. 

As [color=#539595]Scalecommander[/color], avoid chaining a [spell=436335] into a normal [spell=356995] as this will cause you to lose a percentage of the buff equal to how many ticks you clipped.

Clipping is when you cut [spell=356995] short by either interrupting it with another spell or Chaining too early. Currently, clipping non-[spell=436335] [spell=356995] one tick early, by interrupting it for Empowers or [spell=357210] makes very little difference.

[toggler name="Chaining Example" closed=true toc=false]
[center]
Example [spell=356995] channel (imagine this is your castbar):
[table class=grid width=700px style="font-size:100%; line-height:2"]
[tr]

[td background=q2]5 |-------------------------| 4[/td]
[td background=gem6]|-------------------------| 3[/td]
[td background=rep-hated]|-------------------------| 2[/td]
[td background=rep-hated]|-------------------------| 1[/td]

[/tr]
[/table]
Channels go from right to left. The first tick happens when the [spell=356995] is cast. The last tick is when the channel ends.
Between 4 and 5 is [color=green-gem]ok to chain[/color] 

[hr]

Let's assume you chain a second [spell=356995] on the red line.
[table class=grid width=700px style="font-size:100%; line-height:2"]
[tr]

[td background=q2]5 |-------------[color=red-gem]|[/color]-----------| 4[/td]
[td background=gem6]|------------------------| 3[/td]
[td background=rep-hated]|------------------------| 2[/td]
[td background=rep-hated]|------------------------| 1[/td]

[/tr]
[/table]
[pad]
The remainder on this last tick gets carried into the new channel. This means the new [spell=356995] has 6 ticks.
[table class=grid width=800px style="font-size:100%; line-height:2"]
[tr]

[td background=q2]6 |-----------------------| 5[/td]
[td background=gem6]|------------------------| 4[/td]
[td background=rep-hated]|------------------------| 3[/td]
[td background=rep-hated]|------------------------| 2[/td]
[td background=purple]|-------------[color=red-gem]| 1[/color][/td]



[/tr]
[/table]

[/center]
[/toggler]


[/tab]
[/tabs]
[pad]

Our Devastation Evoker guides are always updated with the latest information from in-game experience, simulations, and logs. Make sure to check our changelog for this page by clicking on [b]View Changelog[/b] in the Quick Facts column or on the book icon at the top of the page. If you are interested in more in-depth Devastation Evoker guides for [b]Midnight Season 2[/b], make sure to browse the [i]Navigation Bar[/i] at the top of the page, along with our list of [b]Related Guides[/b] just beneath the [i]Table of Contents[/i].





[tooltip name=GI][color=q]Bank 1 [spell=108853] for [spell=449394], but make sure to use them all before [spell=190319] ends.[/color][/tooltip]
[tooltip name=ScorchHaste][color=q]If you are above 104% haste, don't attempt to get [spell=48108]. 

Cast [spell=133] instead of [spell=2948] if you already have a  [spell=48108].

This is due to extreme Haste breaking Double Pyroblast. The haste value where [spell=2948] stop working can be lower depending on your connection to the server.
[/color][/tooltip]
[tooltip name=ScorchIntoBust][color=q]If you are already casting [spell=133]/[spell=431044] and [spell=190319] is suddenly ready you can use that cast to enter [spell=190319]. [spell=2948] can also be used on the move.
[/color][/tooltip]

[tooltip name=firedup][color=q]Prioritize spending all [spell=108853] charges in [spell=190319] over spending all [spell=269650]. 
[/color][/tooltip]

[tooltip name=pool][color=q]Stop using [spell=108853] charges and [spell=269650] buffs if [spell=190319] will be up soon to ensure they are available during cooldowns. 
[/color][/tooltip]

[tooltip name=sfbust][color=q]If [spell=190319] is ready, hard-cast a spell and activate [spell=190319] right before the cast completes. Priority of spells to hard-cast:
[ul]
[li][spell=11366] with [spell=269650].[/li]
[li][spell=133].[/li]
[li][spell=2948] on the move.[/li]
[/ul]
[/color][/tooltip]

[tooltip name=ffbust][color=q]If [spell=190319] is ready, cast [spell=153561] and activate [spell=190319]. If [spell=153561] isn't avialable, hard-cast a spell and activate [spell=190319] right before the cast completes. Priority of spells to hard-cast:
[ul]
[li][spell=11366] with [spell=269650].[/li]
[li][spell=431044] without [spell=431176].[/li]
[li][spell=2948] on the move.[/li][/ul]
[/color][/tooltip]

[tooltip name=fsbug][color=q]Two simultaneous [spell=2120] casts (one hard-cast, one instant with [spell=195283]) will "munch" the proc and not result in a [spell=195283]. 

Hard-cast [spell=2120] with [spell=48107] [i]only[/i] then consume the generated [spell=195283] after. 

Avoid hard-casting [spell=2120] with [spell=269650] with [spell=195283] already active.
[/color][/tooltip]

[tooltip name=whiffmeat][color=q]The goal here is to proc [spell=269650] before the pull without entering combat.
[/color][/tooltip]

[tooltip name=lastms][color=q]You must activate [spell=190319] in the last 150 milliseconds of the [spell=11366] cast for this opener. 

Distance to the target is also a concern, avoid long travel times. 

[u]Only use this opener only if you are confident in your timing.[/u][/color][/tooltip]

[tooltip name=dblpyro][color=q][spell=133] and the instant [spell=11366] leave your hands at the same time. Both crit. This means you get [spell=195283] for another [spell=11366]. [/color][/tooltip]

[tooltip name=s3tier4p][color=q]The purpose here to proc [spell=1236792] via [spell=359618] as quickly as possible.[/color][/tooltip]

[tooltip name=s3tier4paz][color=q]Generally we want to avoid using [spell=362969] as Flameshaper, but with extreme haste this can get us another Essence Bomb. This GCD is also a good time to [spell=358267] if needed. [/color][/tooltip]


[tooltip name=engulf][color=q][spell=443328] damage on the target is greatly increased by the damage over time (DoT) effects. [spell=365937], [spell=444016], & [spell=357208] must be present when you cast it for optimal gameplay.

[spell=365937] - This DoT comes from [spell=361469]. You only need 1 stack on the target.

[spell=444016] - This DoT comes from [resource=19] spenders. [spell=375087] casts 3 [spell=357211]s which also apply it.

[spell=357208] - With [spell=370819], max rank [spell=357208] so long as you can [spell=443328] while it is active. If [spell=443328] is not ready, use at rank 1. Higher ranks do more damage but make the window smaller.

[spell=370452] and [spell=370867] also further increase the damage of [spell=443328].

 [/color][/tooltip]

[tooltip name=cb][color=q][spell=370455] stacks to 20 and increases damage of [spell=357211]. The exact value of stacks that makes Pyre worth casting depends.

12 stacks is the recommendation at 3 targets. 

Scalecommander gains about 0.3% damage waiting for 16 stacks at 3 targets. The difference in minimal, so 12 is the overall recommendation for the sake of simplicity.

If stacks are available for [spell=375087], they increase the damage of all 3 Pyres it casts. [/color][/tooltip]

[tooltip name=esopener][color=q]You must have enough Haste to still get 4 Empowered spells cast during [spell=375087] for your extensions (via [spell=375797]) for this to be worth it. If your [spell=375087] is less than 38 seconds on the pull, then save [spell=359073] to cast during [spell=375087].[/color][/tooltip]
[tooltip name=openertrinks][color=q]Mastery trinkets like [item=230027] (and new Season 3 ones) are the highest priority here, followed by others effects like [item=232526]. Other trinkets or [item=168973] can also be used here if you have them.[/color][/tooltip]
[tooltip name=tts][color=q][spell=370553] is off the Global Cooldown and can be cast ahead of time. [/color][/tooltip]
[tooltip name=es][color=q]Empowering this spell higher adds more targets. 

Assuming [spell=375757]:
Rank 1: 1-2 Targets
Rank 2: 3-4 Targets
Rank 3: 5-6 Targets
Rank 4: 7-8 Targets ([spell=375783])

[/color][/tooltip]

[tooltip name=scfb][color=q]Empowering this spell increases damage, but shortens the damage over time. 

Rank 1: During [spell=375087]. 
Rank 2: Outside of [spell=375087].
Rank is flexible, and can be increased in AoE or if targets will die soon.

[/color][/tooltip]

[tooltip name=slipstream][color=q]With  [spell=441257], [spell=357210] resets the cooldown on [spell=358267], avoid wasting charges by overcapping.

Hover can be used in place, and can be cast while casting.

[/color][/tooltip]

[tooltip name=scdis][color=q]If you are channeling [spell=436335] and do not have another buff, fully channel [spell=356995] until the end. 

If you have two stacks of [spell=436335], you can chain these casts. 

Chaining means casting another [spell=356995] before the current channel ends, between the penultimate tick and the end of the channel. This transfers remaining bit of progress towards the last tick to the new channel without losing a tick.

[spell=436335] will hit any valid target (in range) in front of your character. Turning your character towards additional targets in cleave will help you get more [spell=436335] hits.
[/color][/tooltip]

[tooltip name=scdis2][color=q][spell=356995] channels can be chained. 

Chaining means casting another [spell=356995] before the current channel ends, between the penultimate tick and the end of the channel. This transfers remaining bit of progress towards the last tick to the new channel without losing a tick. 

Clipping means losing a tick. This can mean you interrupted your [spell=356995] channel with another spell, or chained earlier than the penultimate tick. Clipping is not recommended in most cases, but we will expand on it in the Advanced section.

[/color][/tooltip]

[tooltip name=fsfb][color=q][spell=357208] Damage over time (DoT) should always be applied to enemies, but the duration will quickly disappear with using [resource=19] spenders via [spell=444088]. 

[spell=357208] can be reapplied to targets once the DoT is refreshable, meaning it has <= 30% duration remaining. 



Always use [spell=357208] Rank 1. 

[/color][/tooltip]

[tooltip name=midnights1tier][color=venthyr]Requires Season 1 Midnight tier set ([item-set=1981] ).[/color]
[color=q]
[ul][li]Azure Sweep damage increased by 50% and its damage against your primary target is increased by an additional 100%.[hr][/li]
